rationale: The four CSF cohorts were collected and measured separately, so many proteins probably have a cohort-specific offset. The score is computed within each site, so these offsets add noise and can push the pooled classifier toward between-cohort differences. This change subtracts each protein's per-site mean (from training samples only) after imputation, so the L2 logistic model learns from within-site variation. This uses site only to harmonise features, not as a predictor.

The CSF score is AUROC computed within each of the four cohorts, so differences in protein levels between cohorts are just noise that the pooled logistic regression has to fight against. This version removes each cohort's per-protein median from the log2 data inside `featurize`, so the model only learns the within-cohort contrast that the metric scores. Site is used only for this harmonization and does not need labels.

The four CSF cohorts likely differ in sample handling and MS runs, which adds protein-level offsets that a single pooled linear model has to learn around. The score is within-site AUROC, so I centre each protein on its own site's median (using all items, no labels). This removes those offsets and leaves within-site disease contrasts for the regularized model. Imputation and the classifier are unchanged.

Within each protein, I'll subtract that site's median, computed on the training samples from the same site. This should remove offsets between the four cohorts caused by different pre-analytics and acquisition runs, so the pooled L2 logistic model learns disease-related differences within each site instead of differences between sites. Scoring is within-site, so these offsets add noise without carrying any signal that can be scored. I haven't run this change, so its effect on the Dev score is untested.

I'm adding per-site median centring of each protein. The four CSF cohorts likely differ systematically in pre-analytics and instrument runs, and the score is computed within each site, so removing site location shifts should let the classifier learn the AD-vs-non-AD differences that hold inside a cohort rather than cohort offsets. The centring happens in `featurize` and uses no labels.

CSF cohorts differ in pre-analytics and acquisition, so per-protein site offsets add variance that a pooled linear model has to absorb, even though scoring is done within each site. This change removes each protein's per-site median on the log2 scale (label-free, using `site` only for harmonization) before the same filtering, half-minimum imputation and L2 logistic regression as before. The goal is to make the learned weights reflect within-site AD-vs-non-AD differences.

Data come from four CSF cohorts, and each has its own pre-analytical and instrument offsets. Those offsets distort a pooled linear model, while the score only counts ranking within each site. So I'm adding one change: per-site median centring of every protein (after log2, sample-median centring and half-minimum imputation). This removes cohort shifts and leaves the within-site AD-vs-control contrasts the metric rewards. It only uses `site` for harmonization and never touches labels. To make site centring possible in `featurize`, the ≥70% quantified filter and the half-minimum imputation also move there and now run label-free over all items rather than per training fold.

This change centres each protein's log2 value on its median within its own site (label-free, done in `featurize`, using site only for harmonisation), so the model learns from within-site differences that match how the score is computed.

Data from four CSF cohorts can differ systematically in each protein's level. Scoring is done within site, so these site offsets only add noise for a pooled classifier. I'll centre each protein on its per-site median before imputation and model fitting. Medians come from training samples only, and a test site that never appears in training falls back to its own medians. Site is used only for this harmonization, never as a predictor.

The CSF samples come from four cohorts, and DIA intensities usually carry cohort-specific shifts per protein. Since scoring is within site, those shifts add noise that drowns out the AD signal for the regularized model. This change subtracts each protein's median within its site (on log2, median-centred data), which harmonizes the features without using site as a predictor and without looking at labels.

That way the logistic regression learns AD-vs-non-AD differences that are consistent within sites instead of differences between sites.
